This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act' for short), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 03.09.2018.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 03.09.2018 at 7:30 p.m. he was returning to his native place on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.TS-06/EB- 9821.

When he was in front of Suni Agro Industries on Raichur-Gadwal road, a Tempo Toofaan bearing Reg.No.KA-36-A-3689 (hereinafter referred to as 'offending vehicle' for short) driven by its driver in a rash or negligent manner came from Gadwal side and dashed against the motorcycle of the petitioner.
In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.

Inspite of prolonged treatment,
he is not completely cured.
3.1. After conducting detailed investigation, the concerned police have filed charge-sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the time of accident, he was aged 25 years old and earning Rs.500/- per day.
The offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.2.

As owner and insurer,
both the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 has not filed written statement.

5. Respondent No.2 filed written statement disputing that accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
6.
Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

7. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 15.
8.
On behalf of respondent No.2 one witness examined as RW.1 and Exs.R1 to 4 are marked.

The compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side and prays to allow the appeal.
11. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

12. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.
13.
Based on the complaint lodged in respect of the accident, the concerned police have conducted detailed investigation and filed the charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: Taking into consideration the documents placed on record and the evidence of P.W.1, the Tribunal has rightly held that the accident was occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle.

14. Having regard to the grounds urged in the appeal memo, it is necessary to examine whether the compensation granted to the petitioner is just and reasonable or it calls for interference by this Court.
15.
As per the wound certificate at Es.P4 and discharge summary at Ex.P14 petitioner has sustained isolated transverse fracture of left tibia at middle 1/3rd and other injuries.
He has underwent treatment at Balanku Hospital, Raichur as inpatient from 03.09.2018 to 13.09.2018.
He has also suffered permanent partial disability.

Having regard to the same compensation granted in a sum of Rs.30,000/-
under the head pain & suffering; Rs.10,000/- under the head loss of amenities; Rs.15,000/- under the head food, nourishment and conveyance; and Rs.10,000/- under the head attendant charges is on the lower side. The same are enhanced to Rs.40,000/-, Rs.30,000/-, Rs.25,000/- and Rs.20,000/- respectively.
16. Based on the medical bills, the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.76,000/- and it does not call for any interference.
17. Based on records, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of the petitioner as 25 years and appropriate multiplier 18.
In the absence of proof of exact income, on notional basis, it has considered the income of petitioner as Rs.8,000/-.
Since the accident is of the year 2018, the notional income is considered at Rs.11,750/-.
Having regard to the nature of injuries suffered and avocation of the petitioner, the Tribunal has justified in considering the whole body disability at 9%.
With the income at Rs.11,750/-, 18 multiplier and 9% disability, the loss of future earnings is Rs.11,750/- x 12 x 18 x 9% = Rs.2,28,420/- as against Rs.1,55,520/- granted by the Tribunal.
18. The Tribunal has granted Rs.15,000/- under the head future medical expenses and it is just and reasonable.
Loss of income during laid up period the Tribunal has granted compensation in a sum of Rs.16,000/- the same enhanced to Rs.23,500/-.

19. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.4,57,920/- together with interest at 6% p.a. on the enhanced compensation, as against Rs.3,27,600/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

3. Food, nourishment Rs.15,000/- Rs.25,000/-
 and conveyance 4.
